subject: Data handling & telemetry scope confirmation – follow-up from discovery call
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@averyanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Data handling & telemetry scope confirmation – follow-up from discovery call

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps related to the items you flagged on PII, retention, logging controls, residency, and third-party telemetry: 

Summary of what we heard (from your team):
- Primary use case: document ingestion + summarization for customer support transcripts (contains email addresses, names, some account numbers).
- Regulatory constraints: must keep EU customer data in EU region for EU accounts; US customer data may remain in us-west.
- Concern: telemetry vendors and marketplace integrations that may receive metadata or logs.

Redwood answers (top-level):
- PII handling: We support in-flight token redaction via prompt filters + can configure ingestion pipelines to remove or hash defined PII fields before storage.
- Data residency: Hosted endpoints can be pinned to region (us/eu). For stronger separation we offer Redwood Private where control plane and storage stay in your VPC.
- Retention: Default logs retention is 30 days; we offer configurable retention windows and exportable audit logs for compliance.
- Logging controls: We can disable debug telemetry at the tenant level and provide request-level audit logs (no model KV cache dumps are stored).
- Subprocessors: We maintain a current subprocessor list and can provide the snapshot used for a given contract.

Attachments I’m sharing now (stubs): redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 scope + evidence map), subprocessors-export-2026-11-15.csv (live subprocessor list), telemetry-matrix.xlsx (what telemetry is collected by default vs optional).

Proposed next steps: 
1) Security questionnaire — I’ll have Mina reach out with standard data flow diagram and a single-sheet mapping of PII controls (ETA: EOD 11/16).
2) If the top-level answers are acceptable, schedule a short security deep-dive with your privacy lead and our security engineer (30–45m).
3) We’ll prepare an ingestion example that strips emails and hashes account IDs for a sandbox demo.

Can you confirm availability for a deep-dive next week and whether you prefer Hosted (region-pinned) or a Private deployment for regulated EU traffic?

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary), subprocessors-export-2026-11-15.csv (list), telemetry-matrix.xlsx (matrix)
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@averyanalytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T13:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Data handling & telemetry scope confirmation – follow-up from discovery call

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap and the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side before we loop in privacy/security: 

1) PII ingestion: we cannot send unmasked email addresses or government IDs to third-party models. Can your ingestion pipeline perform deterministic hashing of email addresses and still allow models to surface the hashed identifier in outputs?
2) Residual telemetry: we need assurance that telemetry vendors (e.g., Sentry/Amplitude) will not receive raw PII or request payloads. Is telemetry limited to anonymized metrics by default?
3) Marketplace flows: we have a concern about marketplace connectors (e.g., integrations that ship logs to a partner) — will Redwood Marketplace partners ever pull request bodies or customer-provided content?

We are leaning toward Hosted with regional pinning for now unless the privacy team recommends Private. Available for a 30–45m deep-dive next Tue/Wed afternoon.

— Samantha
Head of Product | Avery Analytics

On Mon, Nov 15, 2026 at 09:12 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Samantha — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap...
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@averyanalytics.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Data handling & telemetry scope confirmation – follow-up from discovery call

Thanks Samantha — quick answers inline and then next steps.

1) Deterministic hashing: Yes — we can hash emails deterministically as part of the ingestion pipeline using a customer-provided pepper (HMAC). That preserves consistent identifiers for model context while preventing reversible PII exposure. We’ll include an example ingestion transform in the sandbox.

2) Telemetry vendors: By default Redwood collects metrics and anonymized traces. Request/response payloads are never sent to third-party telemetry providers unless explicitly enabled by the customer. Marketplace partners cannot read request bodies/content; integrations only receive metadata at most (status codes, latency, tenant id) unless your team enables payload forwarding.

3) Marketplace connectors: Marketplace integrations run under tenant-scoped permissions. Any integration that needs access to content must be explicitly granted by tenant admin — we do not grant blanket read access. For regulated accounts we can disable Marketplace for the tenant entirely.

Attachments: I attached the SOC 2 summary and the subprocessors list we discussed. I also added a short telemetry matrix. See attached.

Planned next steps:
- Mina will share the single-sheet PII controls and a data flow diagram tomorrow (11/16).
- If your privacy lead wants to proceed, let’s schedule Thu 11/18 1:00pm PT for the security deep-dive; I’ll add Marissa for a short demo of the ingestion transform.

Would Thu 11/18 1pm PT work?

Jordan
--
Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, subprocessors-export-2026-11-15.csv, telemetry-matrix.xlsx
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: FW: Data handling & telemetry scope confirmation – internal security notes

Internal notes / suggested language for privacy/security call with Avery: 

- PII: Recommend we propose HMAC hashing with customer-managed salt for emails/account ids. Document acceptable algorithms (SHA-256 HMAC).
- Retention: Offer an SLA option for audit-log exports (30/90/365 days) and note default 30d. If Avery requires >365d, we escalate to legal for contract language.
- Telemetry: Confirm that by default third-party telemetry receives metrics only. For additional assurance, offer a signed statement that request payloads are never forwarded without opt-in.
- Subprocessor control: We can provide a snapshot of subprocessors at signature and 30-day notice for changes. For market integrations that need content access, require a tenant-admin explicit grant and add to contract Exhibit A.

Redlines to prepare for procurement: add Exhibit A (approved subprocessors) + checkbox for Marketplace enablement. Also prepare a minimal security addendum for data residency clauses.

Mina
Director, Security & Privacy | Redwood Inference
